body_en_plain:
M O R E   M A I L ! !

     June, 1992      Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -

 Alan D. Cox..........03    11

 Malcolm Perry........13    26

 Malcolm Goodman......27    33

 Alan D. Cox..........36    44

 Steve Nutting........46    49

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Alan D. Cox, Ostrey Hill,
      ST. CLEARS, Dyfed SA33 4AJ

Dear Brian

First, a bit of a squirm!
Re-reading my letter of 5 April,
I was horrified to see my
comment that I take a relaxed
view on copyright. This, I
hasten to say, only applies to
my own material: if anything I
am perhaps over-zealous with
other people's, as some of my
correspondents can testify!

In an earlier letter I mentioned
software to enable PCs to read
SAM disks. I have now got some
more information: it is Share-
ware and is called ANADISK.

I imagine it is available from
various PC Shareware sources,
but in case of difficulty I can
provide copies for `2.50 post
free (profits to my computer
group). [Write direct to Alan
Cox at the address at the head
of this letter].


I should make two points about
Anadisk: first, it will not read
Apple or Commodore disks (and
hence Amiga) because "they use a
different recording format". I
do not understand exactly what
this means, but no doubt you do.
I do not know for certain that
it can read Atari ST disks, but
since I can with SAM I have no
reason to doubt it can as well.

Secondly, I must point out that
in this role (it also has many
'disk doctor' features) Anadisk
merely reads tracks/sectors into
the PC's memory,like READ AT,and
does nothing about putting them
together in a coherent program/
file: this would need an extran-
eous program in general,although
with a 'fresh' disk where files
are not disjointed there is no
real problem.Thus Anadisk is no-
where near as capable as PCSUITE
which,for example, enables you
to type a SAM BASIC program into
a PC word processor in text form
and turns it into a working SAM
program. An alternative, for
someone who likes to do-it-them-
selves, is to use the MSDOS
DEBUG L command, which acts much
like READ AT.

Having read Kevin Snowdon's
letter in OUTLET 55 I wrote to
him about his comments on RS232.
I asked him about his reference
to remarks by Brian Gaff on the
topic, since I had not seen
them. It turns out they were in
Drivechat in Issue 53 but only
in the Spectrum version. Perhaps
I am unique in being interested
in both SAM and Spectrum, but I
do not want to have to buy both
editions every time, since there
is quite a lot of duplication. I
have brought this up before, and
I know the problem is insoluble.

However, would it be possible to
put a list in the SAM version of
the articles that are only in
the Spectrum version so I could
order up any that took my fancy?

I know you never have any spare
space, but a simple code file
might not be too big.


I imagine B G(aff?) used BTRANS
to move the Spectrum version of
OUTDEX to SAM, or something like
it. I say this because the SAM
version exhibits a couple of
features I have met before using
BTRANS.

First, you can end up with a SAM
program that runs perfectly
satisfactorily but containing
lines that you cannot edit.
Thus, for example, if you EDIT
line 330 in the original then
try to reENTER it, it fails
syntax.

This appears to be due to
"..............etc"( TO 26-LEN
...): I wanted to edit this
line, so I was forced to define
a variable w$=STRING$(34,".").

MasterBASIC does not have this
problem (but, as you have said,
programs that only run under
MasterBASIC are not appropriate
for general use).

I had met this sort of problem
before because Spectrum BASIC
allows keywords to be used as
variable names as well, but of
course SAM BASIC does not. Thus
if you try to edit a line of a
BTRANSed program that uses e.g.,
LEN as a variable ,then you
cannot reENTER it.

(Incidentally, do you know of a
DTRANS i.e. something to read in
a Spectrum BASIC program on a
Disciple/D+ disk then translate
it into a SAM BASIC program? - I
have nearly adapted BTRANS1 to
do this, and will let you have
it if I can get over the final
hurdle, if you are interested).

My second problem was that SAM
BASIC appears to be unable to
edit a line that is so long that
it spills over on to a second
screen page. As an example, I
wanted to remove the GOSUB 195
from the end of your line 60,
but could not. MasterBASIC does
not help here - but I have
recently realised that the
problem is the 'short' screen
with SAM in MODE 4.

I keep coming across irritating
references to the network in the
Technical Manual, but I have
still not managed to get any
volts out of the network pins on
the midi connectors.

I think that you have to use
DEVICE N - followed by a number?
- but even then how do you
indicate who is 'IRIS' and/or do
a network broadcast (assuming it
has similarities with Interface
1)?

        All best wishes,

           Alan D.Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

I may add a note to ADD-ENDERS
in "WHAT ELSE" as to what is in
the Spectrum version exclusively
but I don't know how it will
work out. Every month I seem to
get yet another little job to
worry about! No promises.

String-slicing of a string con-
stant only seems to fail in some
big programs suffering from the
notorious page bug! I think I've
seen it work by putting another
bracket round the string, e.g.,

    PRINT ("TESTING")(TO 4).

If not, delete the rest of the
program, edit the line, SAVE and
reMERGE it back!

Yes, there is a  DTRANS program.
It is on the MGT system disc. It
has been secretly hidden under
the name "dbt.bas" and excluded
from the menu so nobody would
know. It loads some code called
"DTRANS". If it is not on your
copy then write to SAMCo or to
me.

To edit large BASIC lines use
MODE 3 with CSIZE 8,8. You can
get in even more if you use
CSIZE 6,8 or even 6,7 and even
more if you use LISTFORMAT3 from
OUTLET 41.

Hopefully, you will have seen
details in recent OUTLETTERS
about networks although I don't
know what you mean by "IRIS"!
                        - Brian

From:Malcom Perry, KIDDERMINSTER

Dear Brian and Ron,

              TIP:

Just broken the drive connector
for the umpteenth time swapping
drives between Spectrums. My +D
has a firm grip on them and
nothing to hold and pull but the
ribbon. I decided enough is
enough so here is my fix. Take
a length of thin nylon cord of
thickness that just fits nicely
between the pins lengthways on
the +d connector. Plug in the
drive so trapping the cord.
Bring both ends over the top of
the connector and tie in a tight
knot then tie to form a small
loop.

You now have a "handle" that
pulls on the connector and it
can be eased out without having
to put a lot of strain on the
cable.(keep cord in line with
connector so there is a straight
pull.

Obviously this can be used with
any of the IDC drive or printer
connectors and will be added
next time any are removed.


Note however it may not work
with some connectors if the cord
is too thick as there is not
much room between the end of the
plug and socket plastic moulding
so do not force things.

          +2 KEYBOARD:
I seem to recall I saw a
replacement keyboard on the same
stall at a recent show that I
had my colour monitors from. `11
seems to ring a bell but as I
was not looking for keyboards I
did not really take a lot of
notice. Also it may just have
been an odd one. However a phone
call to ALAN at his shop on 0279
433843 by the enquirer would
confirm the position either way.

As regards fitting, the keyboard
comes as a complete, assembled
unit so after removing the case
and unplugging the tails, remove
the screws holding the key unit
to the top cover. Fit the new
unit and replace screws. Plug in
the tails.Do not bend or crease.

One tip is to hold each edge
just above the bared ends and
pull them tightly apart to make
it rigid then gently ease them
into the connectors.

The early tails had strengthen-
ing pieces glued on but later
ones do not so are more fragile.




               SAM

Those that read my serials on
these pages will probably have
gathered that I am not too happy
with having so many faults with
Sams. So,just to keep the record
straight here is an update...

On reporting the last drive pro-
blem on drive 2 (drive 1 having
been back twice),SAMCO said send
the whole computer back and they
would test it all out. They also
stated they would refund the
cost of returning it. So back it
went. A copy of PO receipts also
went to be refunded postage.

Two months later - no SAM, no
refund, no word.

I gave Samco an ultimatum to
supply a SAM that works properly
and pay compensation for extra
costs by a certain date or re-
fund my money.One day before the
deadline I get a letter saying
they'll look into what happened
to my SAM and give me compensat-
ion for all the problems.

It arrived about a week later,no
explanation or anything and they
still had not refunded my costs
as I was promised despite two
further reminders! It was now
three months later.

However, about 10 months after
purchase I now (fingers and
everything else crossed) seem to
have a working SAM. Mind you,
you do need to file the end of
your finger down to fit it
through the slot to be able to
press the disc eject button in
far enough to get the discs out.

It now has SAMCO stickers over
the fixing screws so they cannot
be altered without breaking the
seals - I presume for guarantee
purposes.

To be fair to SAMCO they have
sent me some of the newsdiscs in
lieu of postage paid when
returning the drives previously
but even so I estimate my sam
has cost me about `60 more than
the current price for the
privilege of being unable to
have proper use of the machine
over the last 10 months or so
which does leave a bit of a sour
taste...

             REPAIRS

Now, another story: I recently
had a computer repaired by a
firm in Birmingham. It was
returned and found to still be
faulty. They declined to reply
to correspondence on the matter.

It was repaired elsewhere. The
Z80 they fitted turned out to be
dodgy. On replacement,it all was
O.K. Luckily, it was a plug-in
one - not soldered as most seem
to be.

I asked them for a refund of the
cost of the Z80 but,as expected,
I was ignored. So, like the
recent correspondent in OUTLET I
would be interested in a reli-
able repairer.

This is the second I have used
that turned out to be unsatis-
factory. I do have a firm in
Kidderminster that will do
repairs but they only give a
quote on seeing the computer and
do the repair on a time and cost

basis which is O.K. if you can
personally take it to them and
the repair does not involve too
much work or parts. This is not
really satisfactory for postal
repairs.

However, even some of the "fixed
price" repairers have a small-
print get-out.If the computer is
badly damaged, been got at, or
likely to cost them much over
their fixed price, they can ref-
use to repair - or charge extra.

Some even refuse repair if it
has been repaired previously by
someone else. That's O.K. if
your machine has been yours from
new and you know the history -
but not if you have had it
second hand.

A comment about the SAM SCART
connector and the statement...

 "don't link pins by trial and
 error"

is very valid.Also the following
point is worth mentioning...

There are ready-made SCART leads
that have varying numbers of
pins connected and one that has
all the pins connected to each
end. While I was sorting the
connections for my monitor to
make up a lead it occurred to me
what would be the result if
anyone used a ready-made lead on
being told by the shop "yes it
will work, scart is standard"
- because we all know it ain't!

Leads that only have video,audio
and/or RGB wired would be
unlikely to cause actual damage
but may not work correctly as
has often been mentioned in
these pages.

Even so, if RGB status earth is
wired there is a serious problem
- see below.It is lucky,I think,
that not all earths are connect-
ed but most often one earth is
used for all returns(no doubt to
save cost on type of cable).

The problem could occur if a
lead was used that had all pins
wired though. Pin 12 in the
SCART layout is COMMUNICATIONS
DATA LINE whereas on SAM it is
+5V.

There is a possibility that this
pin,being unlikely to be used on
the monitor, could be connected
to earth for no better reason
than that it was easier to
design the PCB that way. This
would short out the 5v supply.

PIN 18 on SCART is RGB status
earth and is almost 100% to be
connected to earth at the
monitor but at the SAM end this
has +12 on it which would put a
short circuit to earth on the
SAM 12v supply.

These are the two main pins to
be wary of and if using a SCART
lead not supplied specifically
for use with SAM check there is
no connection to pins 12 and 18
at either end.

I think the following statement
that is made in the info
describing SCART advantages that
I have is worth repeating...

  "SCART is a simple connection
  system that the consumer will
  find easy to use"


                 Malcolm Perry

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Perry


You're not the only one with a
sour taste after dealing with
SAMCo - see Malcolm Goodman's
letter and my reply.
                         Brian

From: Malcolm Goodman, LEEDS

In early February of this year I
ordered a printer+disc interface
for my Coupe via Lerm at Whitley
Bay on the basis that they could
get the goods delivered to me
more quickly than if I sent my
order directly to Samco, since
Lerm accept credit cards. Sure
enough,within 2-3 days a package
arrived but was found to contain
a serial-parallel printer inter-
face.

A quick phone call to Lerm
resulted in my returning the
package directly to Samco for a
replacement. Mrs Evans at Lerm
said she would ring Samco so as
to clarify matters.

After some further phone calls
and letters to Samco from yours
truly, the correct item finally
arrived, some four weeks later!


On connecting it up, it failed
to work and I was obliged to
contact Samco by phone to see
what needed doing. It transpired
that an internal link was in the
wrong position, which once
corrected, put me into a 'go
state'.

How much easier and cheaper it
would have been, Samco, if only
you had included a note to the
effect that this is what needed
doing if the unit did not
perform as expected.

Shortly afterwards, on March
23rd, I was pleasantly surprised
to receive a letter signed by
Alan Miles expressing apologies
for the delay and explained that
he was trying to improve the
service.

I quote: "It is my firm ambition
to be able to supply customers
on a next-day basis. The day
after the order is received the
goods should be despatched"
(production delays excepted).

He then goes on:-
"We're not going to send out
acknowledgements. To do so would
be to admit defeat - to say that
we are not likely to perform to
our declared objective of
shipping the day after order".

He continues:-
"Instead, we've developed a
system which will mean that
customers will be notified that
an order has been received and
will be given a reason for delay
if any order is unfulfilled two
weeks from receipt".

It was with this assurance in
mind that, following receipt of
Newsdisk 3, I sent an order for
a 'Kaleidoscope' kit, but after
3 weeks and no kit or that
notification of delay, I felt it
was time to remind Alan Miles of
his letter to me. I simply
requested that if the kit could
not be supplied by return then a
refund of my money was what I
wanted.

At the time of typing this
(14.5.92)no reply to that letter
has been received, but on 2.5.92
the kit arrived.I've now reached
the conclusion that I cannot
rely on Samco since their deeds
do not match their words as far
as I am concerned.


I work at a school which has a
fairly active computer club
which embraces a variety of
machine users - but not a single
SAM amongst them. I would like
to promote the SAM, (because I
think it is a good computer), to
people thinking of a change, but
on the basis of my experiences,
it is not likely to happen.

To quote Alan Miles once more:-
"As a small company competing
against the giants of the
business, I recognise that it's
crucial for us to maintain
strong customer relations - and
we won't do that if we carry on
conducting ourselves as we have
done in your case".

Well, Mr Miles, your company's
(in)actions have now upset me on
three counts, and if you treat
other customers in the same way
as I've been treated, then it
will only be a matter of time
before what I regard as a 'cult'
computer, goes down the same
road as the Oric, Dragon and the
ZX80.
        Malcolm Goodman.

Brian Cavers to Malcolm Goodman

Your experience reflects our own
- with nobs on. I could relate
scores and scores of similar
events but let me just recount
the latest farce.

You might suppose that, as both
media and as software producers,
SAMCo would fall over themselves
to give us better treatment than
the average. If so, God help the
rest of you!

SAMCo have never provided us
with any information for our
readers other than anyone else
can get. When I asked I was told
to ring the Hotline! Now that's
gone there is the Newsdisc...

As soon as we heard about the
Newsdisc we sent SAMCo a cheque
for six month's issues.The first
issue came to us late (priority
was given to other customers for
some reason).

The 2nd issue never arrived.

The 3rd issue never arrived.

I wrote a stiff letter stating
that we needed it EARLY not LATE
so news (about THEIR products)
would be in time for our dead-
line.

We eventually got the two issues
together - the first being six
to seven weeks late - rather
pointless for a "NEWS" disc! No
explanation, apology, nothing.

Well, at least now we shall get
the Newsdiscs.You must be joking
my friend. No sign of the latest
Newsdisc. Sorry, did I say the
"latest"? I meant the MAY issue!

Once I've got this issue to bed
and can find time I shall be
writing to cancel our subscript-
ion and demand a refund. I just
cannot face this hassle every
month. I am utterly, heartily
sick of it quite frankly.

                          Brian

From: Alan D. Cox,
      Pen-y-Maes,Ostrey Hill,
      ST CLEARS, Dyfed SA33 4AJ

Dear Brian,

Re:Networks and Malcolm Perry's
comments,I had tried this myself
but got no volts on the relevant
pins.However,I had always booted
up before I tried, so what I was
getting was Malcolm's 'Network
no longer seems to work!!!' [the
network is disabled when SAMdos
is loaded - BC]

Seems daft to me, but perhaps
this is all a ploy to sell more
copies of MasterDOS (sorry, Andy
- I do not really mean it!) I
shall try again with an unbooted
SAM.

Various points from the May 92
issue: I was interested in the
debate about the date of Easter,
particularly since being an (ex)
mathematician I thought that I
ought to try to respond to the
Hunter/Hughes challenge. Ha,
bloody, ha!

My sources are perhaps the
oddest mixture that I have ever
assembled for a single problem,
viz...

(i) The Book of Common Prayer,
combined with Hymns Ancient and
Modern - my edition is published
by the Cambridge University
Press: it is not dated, but I
know from other evidence that it
was published in about 1938.

(ii) Whittaker's Almanac
(shorter edition) for 1975, and
(iii) The Oxford Companion to
English Literature, Fourth
Edition, dated 1973 - and even
then I still do not have a
realistic answer.

At one level, the determination
of the date of Easter Sunday is
simple - Whittaker points out
that the definition is contained
in an Act of Parliament (24
Geo.II.,cap.23, for those that
understand these things). This
says that Easter-Day is the
first Sunday after the full moon
which happens upon, or next
after, the 21st day of March:
and if the full moon happens
upon a Sunday, Easter-Day is the
Sunday after.

Now you might think this is
quite straightforward, even if
not easy if you do not know
about when full moons occur.

However, Whittaker then goes on
to say that 'The Moon referred
to is not the real moon of the
heavens, but is a hypothetical
Moon on whose "Full" the date of
Easter depends, and the
lunations of this "Calendar"
Moon consist of twenty-nine and
thirty days alternately with
certain necessary modifications
to make the date of its Full
agree as nearly as possible with
that of the real Moon, which is
known as the Paschal Full Moon.

Frankly, at this stage this (ex)
mathematician gives up!!!

It seems to me something akin to
saying that the date of Easter
Sunday is the number you first
thought of!

I would only point out if any-
one wants to check out his/her
algorithm, the Oxford Companion
gives the date of Easter Sunday
from 1066 onwards. Incidentally,
I gather that the interest in
Easter Day for English litera-
ture, which is not obvious to
me, relates to dating historical
events and documents.

Re: Brian Gaff and the datasheet
for the disk controller - I have
Version 3.0 of the Technical
Manual, and Appendix B, pages B1
et seq of my copy is a reprint
of a leaflet VL 1772-02.

Perhaps I need to open SAM up
and check what chip I have got.
I imagine that Brian has all the
leaflets that he needs, but if
he wants a copy of this I would
be happy to send him one.

This reminds me of a point I've
meant to make several times. I
cannot believe your readership
does not include at least one
member of SAMCo's staff so I am
a little disappointed they do
not respond via your columns to
the many points made in them
about SAM and SAMCo - and indeed
about their customer relations
in general. Presumably they want
to keep the Newsdisk as their
exclusive channel,i.e., they are
in fact competing with establ-
ished publications.

I am disappointed so far with
the ROM 'disassembly' in the
SAMCO Newsdisk - I had hoped for
the inclusion of much more
comment - indeed it would be
very useful to have a SAM
equivalent of the Logan/O'Hara
book on the Spectrum ROM.


I note the comments about PROPAC
- I know from my correspondence
with Kevin Snowdon about
Spectrum RS232 ports etc.that he
has had an equally disappointing
response to his PROPAC orders
and is thinking of writing to
you about the problem.The letter
in this month's OUTLET will no
doubt prompt him to do so.

Incidentally, Kevin's efforts
have convinced me that there is
something dreadfully wrong with
my RS232 port - I get vastly
different voltages from those he
measures and I deduce a hardware
fault so I have given up. This
explains why Brian Gaff's
response to my earlier query
baffled me.

        All best wishes,

          Alan D.Cox

Brian Cavers to Alan Cox

We have long since given up on
expecting any support from SAMCo
as we have been producing soft-
ware in support of them since
1988 when they were MGT (on +D/
Disciple) and never had so much
as a note in OUTLETTERS let
alone a useful routine or
program. Yes, I have asked them
but they either do not answer
the letter at all or one of
their favourite tricks is to
answer part of a letter and
ignore the rest.They do not even
send us information about their
products other than what every-
one else gets. In fact, we are
now unable to get their newsdisc
at all (see my reply to Malcolm
Goodman).

No, don't be surprised that they
do not respond to comments about
them in these pages. They don't
bother about reading the likes
of OUTLET - perish the thought!

I have sent copies of critical
letters to them to give them the
opportunity to comment but they
have not even had the courtesy
to acknowledge my letters so I
do not bother any more.

                        - Brian

From: Steve Nutting,
      Steves  Software
      7, Narrow Close,
      Histon, CAMBRIDGE
      CB4 4XX

AMENDMENT TO SC_MONITOR

The files "auto"and "softwriter"
should have the BASIC altered
as:-

610 POKE m+14324+p: POKE
    m+14324+20,p
620 POKE m+14324+1,i,i,i: POKE
    m+14324+1+2-,i,i,i

The above will fix the flashing
colours and weird colours
appearing on the monitor screen
in zones 5 and 6.

Also if you do not like the
character set on SC_MONITOR and
you would like to change it and
you have a copy of SC_ASSEMBLER
256K 1.2 or 512K 1.0 then do the
following:-

Set up the configured Assembler
for the character set you would
like to use . Follow on until
you get to the part of SAVing
the configured Assembler to
disc. Press ESC. Type:-

NEW plus RETURN. Type:-

CLEAR 29999 : POKE 30000,
mem$(457144 TO 457144+1535):
LOAD "moncode"code m:POKE
m+4592,mem$(30000 to 30000+1535)
Then just SAVE out "moncode"CODE
m,32768.

If you are using the 256K
Assembler change 457144 to
96696. The variable m is where
the monitor code starts .

         Steve Nutting

Brian Cavers to Steve Nutting


Thanks, Steve.

I see in your latest advert that
your SC_AUTOBOOT ROM chip does
NOT suffer from the corruption
of discs that the normal ROM
does so may be worth ordering
for that alone! (`15). What's
this about a reset button that
can break into ANY program? Tell
us more!!!!

SC_MONITOR is `15 from Steve's
Software and includes a fast,
advanced disassembler and trace
(single-step) utility.

                        - Brian.

is very valid.Also the following point is worth mentioning...

There are ready-made SCART leads that have varying numbers of pins connected and one that has all the pins connected to each end. While I was sorting the connections for my monitor to make up a lead it occurred to me what would be the result if anyone used a ready-made lead on being told by the shop "yes it will work, scart is standard" - because we all know it ain't!

Leads that only have video,audio and/or RGB wired would be unlikely to cause actual damage but may not work correctly as has often been mentioned in these pages.

Even so, if RGB status earth is wired there is a serious problem - see below.It is lucky,I think, that not all earths are connect- ed but most often one earth is used for all returns(no doubt to save cost on type of cable).

The problem could occur if a lead was used that had all pins wired though. Pin 12 in the SCART layout is COMMUNICATIONS DATA LINE whereas on SAM it is +5V.

There is a possibility that this pin,being unlikely to be used on the monitor, could be connected to earth for no better reason than that it was easier to design the PCB that way. This would short out the 5v supply.

PIN 18 on SCART is RGB status earth and is almost 100% to be connected to earth at the monitor but at the SAM end this has +12 on it which would put a short circuit to earth on the SAM 12v supply.

These are the two main pins to be wary of and if using a SCART lead not supplied specifically for use with SAM check there is no connection to pins 12 and 18 at either end.

I think the following statement that is made in the info describing SCART advantages that I have is worth repeating...

Замечание по поводу разъема SAM SCART и фраза:

> «не соединяйте контакты методом тыка»

совершенно справедливы. Также стоит упомянуть следующий момент...

Существуют готовые кабели SCART с разным количеством распаянных контактов, а также такие, в которых соединены абсолютно все контакты от одного конца до другого. Когда я разбирался с распиновкой для подключения своего монитора, чтобы спаять кабель, я подумал: а что произойдет, если кто-то воспользуется готовым кабелем, поверив словам продавца в магазине: «Да, он будет работать, SCART — это стандарт»? Ведь все мы знаем, что это ни черта не стандарт!

Кабели, в которых распаяны только видео, аудио и/или RGB, вряд ли нанесут реальный ущерб, но могут работать неправильно, о чём уже не раз упоминалось на этих страницах.

Однако если распаяна земля статуса RGB (RGB status earth), возникает серьезная проблема — см. ниже. Считаю, нам ещё повезло, что не все земляные контакты соединены вместе, но чаще всего один общий провод земли используется для всех обратных линий (без сомнения, ради экономии на типе кабеля).

Проблема может возникнуть, если использовать кабель со всеми распаянными контактами. Контакт 12 в стандартной распиновке SCART — это COMMUNICATIONS DATA LINE, тогда как на SAM это +5V.

Существует вероятность, что этот контакт, поскольку он вряд ли будет использоваться на мониторе, может быть соединен с землей просто потому, что так было удобнее развести печатную плату. Это вызовет короткое замыкание по линии питания 5 В.

Контакт 18 на SCART — это земля статуса RGB, и она практически со 100% вероятностью соединена с землей со стороны монитора, но со стороны SAM на этот контакт подаётся +12 В, что приведёт к короткому замыканию 12-вольтовой шины SAM на землю.

Вот два основных контакта, с которыми нужно быть крайне осторожными, и если вы используете кабель SCART, изготовленный не специально для SAM, обязательно убедитесь, что контакты 12 и 18 не подключены ни с одного из концов.

Думаю, стоит повторить следующее утверждение из попавшегося мне рекламного буклета, расписывающего преимущества SCART:

> «SCART — это простая система подключения, чрезвычайно удобная для пользователя»

### ИСПРАВЛЕНИЕ ДЛЯ SC_MONITOR

В файлах «auto» и «softwriter» необходимо изменить строки BASIC следующим образом:

```text
610 POKE m+14324+p: POKE m+14324+20,p
620 POKE m+14324+1,i,i,i: POKE m+14324+1+2-,i,i,i
```

Вышеуказанное исправит мерцание и странные цвета, появляющиеся на экране монитора в зонах 5 и 6.

Кроме того, если вам не нравится набор символов в SC_MONITOR и вы хотите его изменить, и при этом у вас есть копия SC_ASSEMBLER 256K 1.2 или 512K 1.0, выполните следующее:

Настройте сконфигурированный Assembler под тот набор символов, который вы хотите использовать. Продолжайте до тех пор, пока не дойдете до момента сохранения (SAVE) сконфигурированного Assembler на диск. Нажмите ESC. Введите:

NEW и нажмите RETURN. Затем введите:

```text
CLEAR 29999 : POKE 30000,mem$(457144 TO 457144+1535): LOAD "moncode"code m:POKE m+4592,mem$(30000 to 30000+1535)
```

Затем просто сохраните: `SAVE out "moncode"CODE m,32768`.

Если вы используете версию Assembler для 256K, замените 457144 на 96696. Переменная `m` — это адрес, с которого начинается код монитора.
